name: Sel Roti
subtitle: crisp-edged ring of fried fermented rice batter, lightly sweet and cardamom-scented

ingredients.note: some households use water; milk gives a softer crumb inside the crisp shell

prepNotes: Soak the rice in cold water for at least 8 hours, or overnight. It has to be fully softened or the batter will be gritty.
The batter then rests 3-4 hours in a warm spot to ferment. Plan for most of a day, or soak overnight and fry in the afternoon.
Have a wide, deep pan and a long skewer or chopstick ready before you start frying — the rings are turned with the skewer, not tongs.

steps.text: Drain the soaked rice thoroughly and spread it on a cloth for 15 minutes until the surface looks dry.
steps.tip: Wet rice means a slack batter, and slack batter will not hold a ring in hot oil.

steps.text: Grind the rice in batches with the milk and only as much of the water as it takes to move the blades, to a thick, completely smooth batter.
steps.tip: Grind longer rather than adding water. The batter should fall from a spoon in a heavy ribbon.

steps.text: Beat in the sugar, melted ghee, ground cardamom, cloves and salt, then beat by hand for a good 5 minutes.
steps.tip: That beating aerates the batter, and aeration is what gives sel roti its light inside.

steps.text: Cover and leave in a warm place for 3-4 hours, until the batter has risen slightly and smells faintly sweet and sour.
Heat the oil in a kadhai to about 170C — a drop of batter should sink briefly, then rise within 3 seconds.
steps.tip: Too hot and the ring browns before the middle sets; too cool and it drinks oil and goes heavy.

steps.text: Pour the batter into a squeeze bottle or a piping bag. Working quickly, pipe a 12cm ring onto the surface of the oil, joining the ends.
Let it fry undisturbed 1 minute, until it floats free and the top loses its shine.
Turn it with a skewer through the hole and fry another 2 minutes until both sides are a deep reddish gold.
Drain on a wire rack, not paper, and fry the rest one or two at a time.
Cool at least 10 minutes before eating — the crispness only arrives as they cool.

storage: Keeps 3 days at room temperature in a tin, and stays edible for a week. Refresh in a dry pan over low heat for a minute a side; do not refrigerate, which makes them leathery.
